mainTopic: The laws of standing up for a רבי, a father, a ספר תורה and Torah leaders, and the start of מצות עשה שהזמן גרמה
overview: The גמרא teaches that a תלמיד חכם stands for his רבי only morning and evening, so the רבי's honor will not exceed the honor of Heaven. It reconciles this with a ברייתא that an elder should not trouble people. רבי אלעזר warns that a student who does not stand for his רבי is called a רשע, and he learns this through a גזירה שוה of 'פני'. The גמרא then asks whether a son who is his father's teacher must stand for his father, and whether the father must stand for him. It also asks whether a rider counts as walking, and proves from a משנה about a stone with צרעת that he does. A קל וחומר teaches that one stands for a ספר תורה, and a story shows that people busy learning Torah need not stand, though אביי strongly opposed acting that way. רבי אבדימי teaches how long to stand for a חכם, an אב בית דין and a נשיא. Finally the גמרא returns to the משנה's rule about מצות עשה שהזמן גרמה and begins listing examples, a list that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Standing for one's teacher only morning and evening
steps.stepSummary: A תלמיד חכם may stand for his רבי only in the morning and evening, so that his רבי's honor is not greater than the honor of Heaven.
steps.simpleTranslation: A Torah scholar is permitted to stand before his teacher only in the morning and in the evening, so that his teacher's honor will not be greater than the honor of Heaven.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא states a rule: a student stands for his רבי only twice a day, in the morning and in the evening.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Standing is a sign of honor, but it has a limit. If the student stood for his רבי all day, the רבי would be honored more than Heaven itself. So the honor is held to two set times.
steps.whyThisMatters: This rule is the starting point of the whole discussion. Everything that follows tests it.

phrases.english: A Torah scholar is not permitted
to stand before his teacher
except in the morning and evening,
so that his honor should not be
greater than the honor of Heaven.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵין תַּלְמִיד חָכָם רַשַּׁאי לַעֲמוֹד מִפְּנֵי רַבּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opening rule of this section
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A student stands for his רבי only morning and evening, so the רבי's honor will not exceed the honor of Heaven.

steps.title: Bringing a ברייתא that an elder should not trouble people
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא of רבי שמעון בן אלעזר: an elder should not trouble people, learned from 'זקן ויראת'.
steps.simpleTranslation: The גמרא raises an objection: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says, from where do we know that an elder should not trouble people? The פסוק says: 'An elder, and you shall fear.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a challenge by quoting a ברייתא. This step sets up the challenge; the actual attack comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says an elder should not trouble people to stand for him. It reads the words 'elder' and 'you shall fear' next to each other, teaching that the elder too must fear God and not burden others. The גמרא will now show why this seems to clash with step 1.

keyTerms.meaning: They raised an objection (from a תנאי source)
A תנא quoted in the ברייתא

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar says:
From where do we know that an elder should not trouble others?
The verse states: 'An elder, and you shall fear.'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 19:32. The two words sit side by side, so the elder too must fear God and not burden people.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings an outside source to test the rule of step 1
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that standing is only morning and evening
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Set up here; the logic is spelled out in step 3

steps.title: If standing is only twice a day, why worry about trouble?
steps.stepSummary: If standing is only morning and evening, it is an obligation and not a burden. So the ברייתא must mean people stand all day.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say standing is only in the morning and evening, why should the elder not trouble people? It is an obligation! Rather, must it not mean that people stand for him all day?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the challenge: worrying about 'trouble' only makes sense if people stand all day long.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Standing twice a day is a basic duty, so it can't be called a burden that the elder should spare people. The ברייתא's concern suggests standing happens many times a day. That seems to contradict step 1.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, is it not so that

phrases.english: And if you say only morning and evening,
why should he not trouble them?
It is an obligation!
Rather, does it not mean the whole day?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out how the ברייתא of step 2 attacks step 1
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule of step 1 (standing only morning and evening)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A required twice-daily act can't be a 'burden'; the ברייתא's concern implies standing all day

steps.title: Only twice a day, but the elder should still avoid troubling people
steps.stepSummary: Standing really is only morning and evening, but even so the elder should avoid troubling people whenever he can.
steps.simpleTranslation: No; really it is only morning and evening, and even so, as much as he can, he should not trouble them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the rule of step 1 stands. The elder should try to spare people even the twice-daily standing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא is not about standing all day. Even a required standing is some effort, so a considerate elder avoids it when possible. Both sources now fit together.

keyTerms.meaning: As much as he is able

steps.whatToRemember: Standing for one's רבי is only morning and evening, and a considerate elder avoids troubling people even for that.

phrases.english: No, really it is only morning and evening,
and even so,
as much as he is able, he should not trouble them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 3
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterprets the ברייתא as advice to minimize even required honor
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא implies standing all day
steps.terutzMaskana: Standing is twice a day, and the elder should spare people even that when possible

steps.title: A student who does not stand for his teacher is called wicked
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר: a תלמיד חכם who does not stand for his רבי is called a רשע, will not live long, and will forget his learning, based on a פסוק in קהלת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: Any Torah scholar who does not stand before his teacher is called wicked, will not live long, and his learning will be forgotten, as it says: 'And it shall not be well for the wicked, nor will he lengthen his days, like a shadow, because he does not fear before God.'
steps.whatsHappening: A new teaching begins: רבי אלעזר describes the harsh punishment for a student who fails to stand for his רבי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He brings a פסוק that matches each part: 'wicked', 'will not lengthen his days', and 'it shall not be well' (losing his learning). But the פסוק only says 'does not fear before God', so he still needs to show this fear means standing. That comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who gives this teaching

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל תַּלְמִיד חָכָם שֶׁאֵין עוֹמֵד מִפְּנֵי רַבּוֹ
phrases.english: Any Torah scholar who does not stand before his teacher
is called wicked,
and he will not live long,
and his learning will be forgotten,
as it is stated: 'And it shall not be well for the wicked,'
'nor will he lengthen his days, like a shadow,'
'because he does not fear before God.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: כׇּל תַּלְמִיד חָכָם שֶׁאֵין עוֹמֵד מִפְּנֵי רַבּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new teaching on the same subject of standing for one's רבי
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A student who does not stand for his רבי is called a רשע, does not live long, and forgets his learning

steps.title: Showing that this 'fear' means standing
steps.stepSummary: The 'fear' in the פסוק is identified as standing, from the פסוק 'ויראת מאלהיך' in the מצוה of standing for an elder.
steps.simpleTranslation: This fear, I do not know what it is. When it says 'and you shall fear your God', this fear is standing.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר explains why the fear in קהלת means standing: the same idea of fear appears in the מצוה to rise for an elder.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק in ויקרא says to rise before an elder and ends 'and you shall fear your God'. So 'fear' there is connected to standing. That lets רבי אלעזר read the fear in קהלת as standing too.

keyTerms.meaning: I do not know what it is

phrases.english: This fear, I do not know what it is.
When it says: 'And you shall fear your God,'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 19:32, the פסוק that starts 'rise before the elderly'.

phrases.english: this fear is standing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the proof of step 5 by defining 'fear'
steps.raayaObject: That the 'fear' in קהלת 8:13 refers to standing
steps.raayaSupportSource: ויקרא 19:32, where 'ויראת מאלהיך' is part of the מצוה of rising for an elder

steps.title: Why not the fear mentioned with interest or weights?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: maybe the 'fear' in קהלת means the fear mentioned with interest or with weights, not standing.
steps.simpleTranslation: But say it means the fear connected to interest, or the fear connected to weights!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי אלעזר: fear of God appears in other מצוות too, so why link it to standing?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah also speaks of fearing God about taking interest and about honest weights. If the link is only the word 'fear', the קהלת פסוק could be about any of these. So the proof of step 6 seems weak.

phrases.english: But say it is the fear of interest
phrases.notes: ויקרא 25:36. Fearing God is mentioned there too, and also with weights.

phrases.english: or the fear of weights!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the proof in step 6
steps.kashyaTarget: The link between קהלת's 'fear' and standing
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The word 'fear' also appears with interest and weights, so it doesn't point only to standing

steps.title: The link is through the word 'פני'
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר learns the link from the shared word 'פני', which appears with standing but not with interest or weights.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר learns it from 'פני' and 'פני'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי אלעזר is not relying on the word 'fear' but on the word 'פני', which links the two פסוקים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: קהלת says 'מלפני האלהים' and the מצוה of standing says 'והדרת פני זקן'. This shared word makes a גזירה שוה that only fits standing. Interest and weights don't share this word, so the challenge falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: Linking two פסוקים through a shared word

steps.whatToRemember: A student who does not stand for his רבי is called a רשע; this is learned from a גזירה שוה of 'פני' between קהלת and the מצוה of rising for an elder.
steps.confusionAlert: The link is not the word 'fear', which appears in many places. It is the word 'פני', found in both פסוקים.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar:
learns from 'פני' and 'פני'.
phrases.notes: קהלת has 'מלפני' and ויקרא 19:32 has 'פני זקן', the same word in both.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 7
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifies the real link as a גזירה שוה on a different word
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The link was the word 'fear', which could point to interest or weights
steps.terutzMaskana: The link is 'פני', found only with standing for an elder

steps.title: Must a son who teaches his father stand for him?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether a son who is his father's teacher must stand for his father.
steps.simpleTranslation: A question was asked: if a son is also his father's teacher, does he have to stand up for his father?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question about two kinds of honor clashing: honor of a father and honor of a teacher. This sets up the proof that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a son stands for his father, and a student stands for his teacher. Here the son is the teacher, so the father is his student. The question is whether being the father's רבי removes the son's duty to stand.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was raised before them (the scholars)
His son who is also his teacher
To stand up before someone (as a sign of respect)

phrases.english: A question was asked of them:
A man's son who is also his teacher,
what is the law about standing before his father?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from standing for a רבי or elder to a new case where a father and a teacher are the same pair of people.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does a son who is his father's teacher have to stand for his father?

steps.title: שמואל told רב יהודה to stand for his father
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a story where שמואל told his student רב יהודה, a great scholar, to stand for his father.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: שמואל said to רב יהודה, 'Sharp one, stand up for your father.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to answer the question with a story about שמואל and רב יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יהודה was a greater scholar than his father רב יחזקאל, so he counts like his father's teacher. Since שמואל still told him to stand, it looks like a son who is his father's teacher must stand.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear (a proof is coming)
Sharp-toothed one, a fond nickname for רב יהודה

phrases.english: Come and hear,
for שמואל said to רב יהודה:
Sharp-toothed one,
phrases.notes: A loving nickname שמואל used for his sharp student רב יהודה.

phrases.english: stand up before your father.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע, דַּאֲמַר לֵיהּ שְׁמוּאֵל לְרַב יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a proof to answer the question of step 9.
steps.raayaObject: That a son who is greater in Torah than his father must still stand for him.
steps.raayaSupportSource: שמואל's instruction to רב יהודה to stand for his father רב יחזקאל.

steps.title: רב יחזקאל was a special case
steps.stepSummary: The proof is rejected: רב יחזקאל was a man of great deeds, so even שמואל stood for him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יחזקאל is different, because he was a man of good deeds; even שמואל himself would stand for him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes away the proof by saying רב יחזקאל deserved standing for his own greatness, not just because he was a father.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If even שמואל, the great teacher, stood for רב יחזקאל, then רב יהודה standing for him tells us nothing about the general rule. So the original question stays open.

keyTerms.meaning: Is different (this case cannot teach the rule)

phrases.english: רב יחזקאל is different,
phrases.notes: רב יחזקאל was רב יהודה's father.

phrases.english: for he was a man of good deeds,
so that even מר שמואל too
would stand before him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of step 10.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof only; it does not decide the question either way.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רב יחזקאל earned standing on his own merit, so the story says nothing about an ordinary father whose son is his teacher.
steps.confusionAlert: The question from step 9 is never actually answered. The proof is just removed, and the גמרא moves on.

steps.title: So why did שמואל say it?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if everyone stood for רב יחזקאל anyway, what was שמואל telling רב יהודה?
steps.simpleTranslation: But then what was שמואל telling him?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a follow-up: if standing for רב יחזקאל was obvious, why did שמואל need to say it? This sets up the explanation that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the story is not about the father-teacher rule, שמואל's words seem pointless. The גמרא needs to find a new point in them.

keyTerms.meaning: But then what was he telling him?

phrases.english: But then what was he telling him?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows from the rejection in step 11, which left שמואל's words seemingly without purpose.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What was the point of שמואל's instruction, if it was not about the father-teacher rule?

steps.title: Stand even when I don't notice him
steps.stepSummary: שמואל meant: sometimes your father comes from behind me, so I don't stand; you should stand anyway and not worry about my honor.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what he was telling him: sometimes your father comes from behind me. You stand for him, and don't worry about my honor.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that שמואל's words were a practical instruction, not a rule about a son who teaches his father.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל might not see רב יחזקאל coming from behind him. רב יהודה might hold back from standing so that he would not stand while his teacher stays seated. שמואל tells him to stand anyway.

phrases.english: This is what he was telling him:
Sometimes he comes from behind me,
phrases.notes: So שמואל doesn't see רב יחזקאל coming and doesn't stand up.

phrases.english: you stand up before him
and don't worry about my honor.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 12.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שמואל's words seemed pointless once the story was not about the father-teacher rule.
steps.terutzMaskana: שמואל was telling רב יהודה to stand even when שמואל himself didn't see the father coming, without worrying about שמואל's honor.

steps.title: Must a father stand for a son who teaches him?
steps.stepSummary: A second question: must the father stand for his son when the son is his teacher?
steps.simpleTranslation: A question was asked: if a son is also his father's teacher, does the father have to stand up for his son?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא flips the question around: now it asks about the father's duty, not the son's.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A student stands for his teacher, so the father, as the student, should stand. But it may be improper for a father to stand for his own son. The question is which consideration wins.

keyTerms.meaning: That his father should stand before him

phrases.english: A question was asked of them:
A man's son who is also his teacher,
what is the law about the father standing before him?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The reverse of the question in step 9.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does a father have to stand for his son when the son is his teacher?

steps.title: רבי יהושע בן לוי stood only for the נשיא's honor
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי said he would not stand for his son except out of honor for the household of the נשיא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: רבי יהושע בן לוי said, 'It is not proper for me to stand for my son, except out of respect for the household of the נשיא.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a statement of רבי יהושע בן לוי about standing for his own son. The exact proof from it is drawn in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהושע בן לוי says that, on his own, his son does not deserve his standing. He stands only because the son is connected to the נשיא's family.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not proper for me
The honor of the household of the נשיא

phrases.aramaic: תָּא שְׁמַע דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי:
phrases.english: Come and hear, for רבי יהושע בן לוי said:
It is not proper for me
to stand before my son,
except because of the honor of the household of the נשיא.
phrases.notes: His son was connected to the נשיא's family, so he stood out of respect for that family.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source to answer the question of step 14.
steps.raayaObject: Whether a father stands for a son who is his teacher.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יהושע בן לוי's statement about standing for his son.

steps.title: Inference: if my son were my teacher, I would stand
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא infers that he refused only because he was his son's teacher; if the son were his teacher, he would stand.
steps.simpleTranslation: The reason he did not have to stand is that he was his son's teacher. But if the son were his teacher, he would stand for him!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws the proof from רבי יהושע בן לוי's words: a father does stand for a son who is his teacher.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא reads 'not proper' as meaning 'because I am greater than him.' That suggests that if the son were greater, the teacher, the father would have to stand. This would answer the question of step 14 with a yes.

phrases.english: The reason is that I am his teacher,
but if he were my teacher,
I would stand before him!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the proof hidden in the statement of step 15.
steps.raayaObject: That a father must stand for a son who is his teacher.
steps.raayaSupportSource: An inference from רבי יהושע בן לוי's words that he was not obligated only because he was his son's teacher.

steps.title: Even if my son were my teacher, I wouldn't stand
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rereads the statement: even if the son were his teacher, the father would not stand, because he is the father.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what he meant: it is not proper for me to stand for my son, even if he were my teacher, since I am his father. I stand only out of respect for the household of the נשיא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the inference by explaining רבי יהושע בן לוי's words a different way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Not proper' is not because he is the teacher. It is because he is the father, and that reason holds even if the son were his teacher. On this reading, the statement teaches that a father does not stand for his son.
steps.whatToRemember: Son who teaches his father: the proof that he must stand is pushed aside, since רב יחזקאל was special. Father whose son teaches him: on the final reading of רבי יהושע בן לוי, being the father means he doesn't stand, except for some outside honor like the נשיא's household.

phrases.english: This is what he meant:

phrases.aramaic: אֲנִי אֵינִי כְּדַי לַעֲמוֹד מִפְּנֵי בְנִי
phrases.english: It is not proper for me to stand before my son
even if he were my teacher,
since I am his father,
except because of the honor of the household of the נשיא.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכִי קָאָמַר: אֲנִי אֵינִי כְּדַי לַעֲמוֹד מִפְּנֵי בְנִי וַאֲפִילּוּ הוּא רַבַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the inference of step 16 by rereading step 15's source.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the inference that the father would stand if the son were his teacher.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The reason for not standing is being the father, not being the teacher, so it applies even when the son is the teacher.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a father's honor may outweigh a teacher's honor when the same son is both, unless some outside honor, like the נשיא's family, is involved.

steps.title: Is riding the same as walking?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether someone riding on an animal counts as 'walking' or not.
steps.simpleTranslation: A question was asked: is a person who is riding considered like a person who is walking, or not?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question about standing up: does a rider count as someone who is walking? This sets up the proof that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A rider is carried by the animal, so his body is moving, but he himself is sitting still. The question is which one counts: the movement of the animal, or the stillness of the rider.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was asked among them (an open question)
Is considered like / is equal to

phrases.english: A question was raised before them:
Is one who is riding considered like one who is walking,
or not?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ: רָכוּב כִּמְהַלֵּךְ דָּמֵי, אוֹ לָא?
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the father-and-son question and opens a new question about standing up.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does riding count as walking or as sitting still?

steps.title: אביי brings the משנה of the impure person under a tree
steps.stepSummary: אביי quotes a משנה: if a טמא sits under a tree, a טהור person there becomes impure; if the טמא only stands, the טהור stays pure. The same rule applies to a stone with צרעת.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Come and hear: if an impure person sits under a tree and a pure person stands there, the pure one becomes impure. If the impure one stands under the tree and the pure one sits, he stays pure. But if the impure one sat down, the pure one becomes impure. And the same is true for a stone with צרעת.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי brings a משנה about a מצורע under a tree to help answer the question. The actual lesson is drawn in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A מצורע makes others impure under the same covering only when he settles in one place, by sitting. If he is just standing, he is like someone passing through and does not make them impure. The stone with צרעת follows the same rule, which is the key to the proof.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear (a proof is coming)
Tree (its branches act like a roof)
A stone with a צרעת mark

phrases.english: Abaye said: Come and hear:
If an impure person is sitting under the tree,
phrases.notes: The 'impure person' here is a מצורע, who makes people under the same roof impure.

phrases.english: and a pure person is standing there, he becomes impure.
If the impure person is standing under the tree
and the pure person is sitting, he stays pure,
but if the impure one sat down, the pure one becomes impure.
And the same is true with a stone that has a צרעת mark.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source to answer the question of step 18.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in נגעים about a טמא and a stone with צרעת under a tree

steps.title: Riding counts like walking
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר כהן learns from the stone case that being carried counts as moving, and the גמרא concludes that riding is like walking.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב נחמן בר כהן said: This shows that riding is considered like walking. Learn from it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר כהן explains what the stone case proves, and the גמרא accepts it as the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The stone does not move by itself. It is carried by a person who is standing, so it is 'riding' on him. Since it does not make others impure, it counts as moving, so riding is like walking.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from it (the point is proven)

steps.whatToRemember: A person riding counts like someone walking. The proof is the stone with צרעת: when it is carried by a standing person, it counts as moving.

phrases.english: And Rav Naḥman bar Kohen said:
This is to say
that riding is considered like walking,
phrases.notes: The stone is 'riding' on the person carrying it. When he stands, it counts as moving and does not make others impure.

phrases.english: Conclude from it.

steps.triggerLanguage: זֹאת אוֹמֶרֶת רָכוּב כִּמְהַלֵּךְ דָּמֵי, שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion from the משנה quoted in step 19.

steps.title: Must one stand for a ספר תורה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks a new question: is there a duty to stand up for a ספר תורה?
steps.simpleTranslation: A question was asked: what is the law about standing up for a ספר תורה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question about standing up, this time for a ספר תורה instead of a person. The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now, all the rules of standing up were about people: a חכם, an elder, a father. Now the גמרא asks whether the same honor applies to the Torah scroll itself.

keyTerms.meaning: To stand up for (out of respect)

phrases.english: A question was raised before them:
What is the law about standing up before a Torah scroll?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ: מַהוּ לַעֲמוֹד מִפְּנֵי סֵפֶר תּוֹרָה?
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new question after the riding question was settled.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is there a duty to stand up for a ספר תורה?

steps.title: A קל וחומר: we stand for the Torah itself
steps.stepSummary: רבי חלקיה, רבי סימון and רבי אלעזר answer with a קל וחומר: if we stand for people who learn Torah, we certainly stand for the Torah.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חלקיה, רבי סימון and רבי אלעזר say: it is a קל וחומר. If people stand up for those who learn the Torah, then for the Torah itself, all the more so!
steps.whatsHappening: Three אמוראים answer the question with a קל וחומר: yes, one must stand for a ספר תורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We stand for a תלמיד חכם only because of the Torah he learns. So the Torah itself, which is the reason for that honor, surely deserves at least the same respect.
steps.whatToRemember: One must stand up for a ספר תורה, learned by a קל וחומר from standing up for people who learn Torah.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי חִלְקִיָּה וְרַבִּי סִימוֹן וְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אָמְרִי:
phrases.english: Rabbi Ḥilkiya and Rabbi Simon and Rabbi Elazar say:
It is an a fortiori (how much more so) argument:
If people stand up before those who learn it,
phrases.notes: 'It' means the Torah. These are the תלמידי חכמים we stand for.

phrases.english: then before it itself, is it not all the more so?!

steps.triggerLanguage: קַל וָחוֹמֶר, מִפְּנֵי לוֹמְדֶיהָ עוֹמְדִים – מִפָּנֶיהָ לֹא כׇּל שֶׁכֵּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question raised in step 21.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Yes, one must stand for a ספר תורה, by a קל וחומר from standing for those who learn Torah.

steps.title: Two scholars stand up for רבי שמעון בר אבא
steps.stepSummary: A story begins: רבי אלעאי and רבי יעקב בר זבדי were sitting, רבי שמעון בר אבא passed by, and they stood up for him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעאי and רבי יעקב בר זבדי were sitting. רבי שמעון בר אבא walked past, and they stood up for him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story connected to the topic of standing out of respect. This step sets the scene for רבי שמעון בר אבא's reaction in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing is ruled yet. We only learn that two scholars stood up for a passing scholar, which is the action he will question next.

keyTerms.meaning: were sitting (often means sitting and learning)

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אִלְעַי וְרַבִּי יַעֲקֹב בַּר זַבְדִּי הֲווֹ יָתְבִי.
phrases.english: Rabbi Ilai and Rabbi Yaakov bar Zavdi were sitting.

phrases.aramaic: חָלֵיף וְאָזֵיל רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בַּר אַבָּא,
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon bar Abba was passing by,
and they stood up before him.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אִלְעַי וְרַבִּי יַעֲקֹב בַּר זַבְדִּי הֲווֹ יָתְבִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the קל וחומר about standing for a ספר תורה, the גמרא brings a story about standing for a scholar.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Two scholars stood for a passing scholar; the halachic point comes in the next step.

steps.title: Two reasons they did not need to stand
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בר אבא tells them they did not need to stand: they are higher in rank than him, and people learning Torah do not stand for its students.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: First, you are full חכמים and I am only a חבר. Second, does the Torah stand up for the people who learn it?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון בר אבא gives two reasons why the scholars should not have stood for him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His first reason is about rank: a higher scholar does not stand for a lower one. His second reason turns around the logic of step 22. While you are busy learning, you are connected to the Torah itself, and the Torah does not stand for its own students.

keyTerms.meaning: an associate scholar, lower in rank

steps.confusionAlert: In step 22 we stood for a ספר תורה because we stand for its students. Here the reasoning runs the other way: the Torah, which those busy learning are connected to, does not stand for its students.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לְהוּ: חֲדָא – דְּאַתּוּן חַכִּימֵי וַאֲנָא חָבֵר.
phrases.english: He said to them: One, you are scholars and I am an associate.
phrases.notes: A חבר here is someone who had not received full סמיכה, so he ranked lower than them.

phrases.aramaic: וְעוֹד, כְּלוּם תּוֹרָה עוֹמֶדֶת מִפְּנֵי לוֹמְדֶיהָ.
phrases.english: And furthermore, does Torah stand before those who learn it?
phrases.notes: He means: you were in the middle of learning, so you did not need to stand.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the speaker's response to the standing described in step 23.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A higher-ranked scholar need not stand for a lower one, and someone busy learning Torah need not stand for a scholar.

steps.title: His view matches רבי אלעזר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא connects רבי שמעון בר אבא's second reason to רבי אלעזר, who rules that a student may not stand for his teacher while learning Torah.
steps.simpleTranslation: He holds like רבי אלעזר, who said: a תלמיד חכם may not stand for his teacher while he is busy learning Torah.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא identifies the source of the second reason: it is the view of רבי אלעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר goes further than "you don't need to": he says a student is not allowed to stand. Stopping to honor a person would take away from the honor of the Torah he is learning.

phrases.english: He holds like Rabbi Elazar.
As Rabbi Elazar said:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין תַּלְמִיד חָכָם רַשַּׁאי לַעֲמוֹד מִפְּנֵי רַבּוֹ
phrases.english: A Torah scholar is not permitted to stand before his teacher
at a time when he is busy learning Torah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finds the source behind the second reason in step 24.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי אלעזר, a student may not stand for his teacher while he is learning Torah.

steps.title: אביי strongly opposes this practice
steps.stepSummary: אביי curses anyone who acts according to רבי אלעזר's ruling.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי cursed this practice.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reports that אביי strongly rejected acting on רבי אלעזר's ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי does not argue with the logic. He rejects it in practice, because a student who stays seated before his teacher looks like he is disrespecting him. In real life, this pushes back against not standing.

keyTerms.meaning: on it (on this ruling or practice)

steps.whatToRemember: There are two sides here. רבי אלעזר says a student busy learning should not stand for his teacher. אביי strongly opposed acting that way.

phrases.english: Abaye cursed over it.
phrases.notes: He means he cursed anyone who actually follows this ruling and stays seated before his teacher.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reacts strongly against the ruling of רבי אלעזר brought in step 25.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects acting on רבי אלעזר's ruling in practice.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Staying seated before one's teacher looks like disrespect.

steps.title: A disagreement about the people watching משה
steps.stepSummary: רבי אמי and רבי יצחק נפחא disagree about the פסוק "they looked after משה until he went into the tent": one reads it as criticism, the other as praise.
steps.simpleTranslation: About the פסוק "And they looked after משה until he came into the tent": רבי אמי and רבי יצחק נפחא disagree. One says it is said as criticism, and one says it is said as praise.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new discussion about a פסוק that describes the people watching משה walk by.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two אמוראים disagree about how to read the people's watching. One sees it as something bad, and the other as a good thing. The next steps explain each side.

keyTerms.meaning: as criticism, in a bad way

phrases.english: "And they looked after Moses until he came into the tent,"
Rabbi Ami and Rabbi Yitzchak Nappacha [disagree].

phrases.aramaic: חַד אָמַר לִגְנַאי, וְחַד אָמַר לְשֶׁבַח.
phrases.english: One said it is as criticism, and one said it is as praise.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהִבִּיטוּ אַחֲרֵי מֹשֶׁה עַד בֹּאוֹ הָאֹהֱלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new discussion about standing for leaders, based on a פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There is a disagreement about whether the people watching משה is criticism or praise.

steps.title: Explaining each side of the disagreement
steps.stepSummary: The criticism view is explained the way it is known elsewhere. The praise view is explained by a teaching that חזקיה is about to bring.
steps.simpleTranslation: The one who says it is criticism explains it the way it is known. The one who says it is praise explains it like the teaching חזקיה said:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא briefly explains each side and sets up the teaching that will explain the praise view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The criticism reading is not spelled out here. The praise reading depends on the הלכה of standing, which comes in the next step.

phrases.english: The one who says it is criticism: as it is.
phrases.notes: The גמרא assumes we already know the negative explanation from elsewhere, so it does not repeat it here.

phrases.english: The one who says it is praise:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the two sides of the disagreement in step 27.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The praise reading is based on the teaching that comes next.

steps.title: How long to stand for a חכם and an אב בית דין
steps.stepSummary: Through a chain of teachers, רבי אבדימי of Haifa teaches: for a passing חכם you stand within four אמות. For an אב בית דין you stand as soon as you see him. In both cases you sit once he has passed four אמות.
steps.simpleTranslation: חזקיה said: רבי חנינא, son of רבי אבהו, told me in the name of רבי אבהו, in the name of רבי אבדימי of Haifa: When a חכם passes, you stand before him for four אמות, and once he has passed four אמות you sit. When an אב בית דין passes, you stand as soon as he is in sight, and once he has passed four אמות you sit.
steps.whatsHappening: חזקיה brings the teaching that explains the praise view. It sets out how long to stand for different levels of leaders.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The higher the person's rank, the earlier you start standing. For a חכם you stand only when he is close, within four אמות. For an אב בית דין you stand as soon as you see him. For both, you may sit once he has gone four אמות past you.

keyTerms.meaning: as far as his eyes can see

phrases.english: Chizkiyah said:

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לִי רַבִּי חֲנִינָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי אֲבָהוּ,
phrases.english: Rabbi Chanina, son of Rabbi Abbahu, told me,
Rabbi Abbahu said,
Rabbi Avdimi of Haifa said:

phrases.aramaic: חָכָם עוֹבֵר – עוֹמֵד מִלְּפָנָיו אַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת,
phrases.english: A scholar passing: one stands before him within four cubits,
and once he has passed four cubits, he sits.

phrases.aramaic: אַב בֵּית דִּין עוֹבֵר – עוֹמֵד מִלְּפָנָיו מְלֹא עֵינָיו,
phrases.english: The head of the court passing: one stands before him as soon as he is in sight,
and once he has passed four cubits, he sits.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר חִזְקִיָּה: אֲמַר לִי רַבִּי חֲנִינָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי אֲבָהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the teaching that step 28 said would explain the praise view.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For a חכם, stand within four אמות. For an אב בית דין, stand as soon as he is in sight. In both cases, sit after he has passed four אמות.

steps.title: For a נשיא you stand until he sits down
steps.stepSummary: For a נשיא you stand from when he comes into sight until he sits in his place. This is learned from the people watching משה until he entered the tent, so the פסוק is praise.
steps.simpleTranslation: When a נשיא passes, you stand as soon as he is in sight, and you do not sit until he sits in his place. As it says: "And they looked after משה until he came into the tent."
steps.whatsHappening: The teaching reaches its highest level, the נשיא, and brings the פסוק as its source. This completes the praise reading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike the earlier levels, for a נשיא you keep standing until he is seated in his place. The people kept watching (standing) until משה entered the tent, which shows they were giving him the full honor due a נשיא. That is why this view reads the פסוק as praise.

keyTerms.meaning: the head of the Sanhedrin, the top leader
as it is said (introduces a פסוק)

steps.whatToRemember: There are three levels of standing. For a חכם: from four אמות away until four אמות after he passes. For an אב בית דין: from when he is in sight until four אמות after he passes. For a נשיא: from when he is in sight until he sits in his place. The last rule comes from the people watching משה, which is why one view reads that פסוק as praise.
steps.whyThisMatters: This teaching is the basis for the הלכה of how long one must stand for different levels of Torah leaders.

phrases.aramaic: נָשִׂיא עוֹבֵר – עוֹמֵד מִלְּפָנָיו מְלֹא עֵינָיו,
phrases.english: The Nasi passing: one stands before him as soon as he is in sight,
and he does not sit until he [the Nasi] sits in his place,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״וְהִבִּיטוּ אַחֲרֵי מֹשֶׁה עַד בֹּאוֹ הָאֹהֱלָה״.
phrases.english: as it is said: "And they looked after Moses until he came into the tent."
phrases.notes: שמות 33:8, the same פסוק from step 27.

steps.triggerLanguage: נָשִׂיא עוֹבֵר – עוֹמֵד מִלְּפָנָיו מְלֹא עֵינָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבי אבדימי's teaching with the highest level and its source, closing the praise reading of step 27.
steps.raayaObject: That one stands for a נשיא until he sits in his place, and that the פסוק describes praise.
steps.raayaSupportSource: שמות 33:8: "וְהִבִּיטוּ אַחֲרֵי מֹשֶׁה עַד בֹּאוֹ הָאֹהֱלָה"
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: For a נשיא, one stands from when he comes into sight until he sits in his place, as the people did for משה.

steps.title: Returning to the next line of the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's rule about מצות עשה שהזמן גרמה to start a new topic.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'Every positive מצוה that is caused by time, etc.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא leaves the topic of standing for חכמים and goes back to the משנה. It quotes the next line, which says women are exempt from time-bound positive מצוות. This is a setup line that gets us ready for the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Quoting the opening words of a משנה line tells us a new section is starting. The topic now moves from honoring parents and חכמים to which מצוות women are exempt from.

keyTerms.meaning: A 'do' מצוה that applies only at certain times (literally: 'that time causes it')
'Etc.', meaning the rest of the line continues

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל מִצְוַת עֲשֵׂה שֶׁהַזְּמַן גְּרָמָהּ וְכוּ׳.
phrases.english: Every positive מצוה caused by time, etc.
phrases.notes: The 'etc.' points to the rest of the משנה's line: women are exempt from these מצוות.

steps.triggerLanguage: כׇּל מִצְוַת עֲשֵׂה שֶׁהַזְּמַן גְּרָמָהּ וְכוּ׳
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the long section on standing for חכמים and parents (steps 1–30) and goes back to the משנה's next rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Women are exempt from every מצות עשה שהזמן גרמה, as the משנה stated.

steps.title: A ברייתא gives examples of time-bound positive מצוות
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא asks what a מצות עשה שהזמן גרמה is and answers with examples: סוכה, לולב, שופר, ציצית.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: Which is a positive מצוה caused by time? סוכה, לולב, שופר, and ציצית.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to show what the משנה means by a time-bound positive מצוה. The ברייתא lists real examples.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה gave only a general category. The ברייתא makes it concrete: each מצוה on the list has a set time when it applies, so women are exempt from it. The question inside the ברייתא is not a challenge. It is just the ברייתא's way of starting its list.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The Rabbis taught', which opens a ברייתא
Living in the booth on סוכות
Taking the palm branch on סוכות
Blowing the ram's horn on ראש השנה

steps.confusionAlert: Don't read 'איזוהי' as the גמרא attacking the משנה. It is the ברייתא's own question, used only to introduce the examples.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
Which is a positive מצוה caused by time?
סוכה, and לולב, שופר, and ציצית,

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: אֵיזוֹהִי מִצְוַת עֲשֵׂה שֶׁהַזְּמַן גְּרָמָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines the category the משנה named in step 31 by giving examples.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: סוכה, לולב, שופר, and ציצית are examples of מצות עשה שהזמן גרמה, which women are exempt from.
